_what: Dimensions for the retrofit model. Almost all STATED: this is a drawn arrangement, not a design, and the kinds say which is which.

_measured_context.source: scripts/architecture.py, from the municipal sewer-catchment layer and the OSM road extract

params.label: Shaft spacing (one bore shot)
params.note: The shot runs shaft to shaft. Danish street manholes sit closer than a bore's reach, so spacing is set by the shafts that exist, not by the method.

params.label: Cover to the crown of the rain line
params.note: Frost and traffic load set the minimum. Below this the line freezes in a sag; above it, the rain line starts to compete with the sewer for depth.

params.label: Rain line, internal diameter
params.note: The variable this page exists to argue about. Sized for the frequent rain, not for the cloudburst - the surface network takes that. The panel above computes the smallest diameter that both carries the flow and still scours, so the slider can be checked against it: bigger is not safer here, it is slower.

params.label: Rain line gradient
params.note: Guided boring can hold a grade; free-steered drilling cannot, which is what makes this number decide the method. It also decides whether the line cleans itself: velocity goes with the square root of it. The rule of thumb for a minimum is 1/D in millimetres - 4 per mille for a DN250 - and the head of a network usually needs more than that because the flow there is small. Watch the fall per shot in the model: at 80 m, 8 per mille costs 640 mm of depth every shot, which is depth the line does not have to give.

params.label: Existing combined sewer, internal diameter
params.note: Typical of an inner-city Copenhagen combined sewer. It was sized for rain, which is why it is too big for sewage once the rain leaves.

params.label: Existing sewer invert, below street
params.note: Deep enough to take house drains by gravity. The rain line has to fit above it without touching what else is in the first metre.

params.label: Foul bore, if the sewer is lined down
params.note: The fourth arrangement: a pipe sized for the stream it carries, pulled through the pipe that is already there.

params.label: House drain
params.note: Unchanged in every arrangement but the swapped one, which is what makes the swapped one slow.

params.label: Shaft, internal diameter
params.note: A standard concrete chamber. It has to hold a person, a ladder and now a pan that lifts.

params.label: Impervious area drained to this shot
params.note: Derived, not assumed: 1,296 km of street inside the combined catchments drains 3,447 impervious hectares, so a metre of street carries about 26.6 m² and a shot's worth is the default here. A line near the outlet of a catchment carries many shots' worth, which is what the slider is for.

params.label: Design rain
params.note: Ordinary heavy rain, well under a cloudburst. The reanalysis record cannot resolve an hour this wet, which is a limit of the instrument rather than of Copenhagen.

params.label: Runoff coefficient
params.note: Paved surface. Roofs are higher, gardens far lower.

params.label: Manning roughness of the new line
params.note: Smooth-bore plastic, fused joints. A concrete sewer is nearer 0.013 and an old brick one worse than that.

params.label: Self-cleansing velocity
params.note: The velocity at which a gravity line carries its own grit rather than laying it down. The design condition is that it is reached at a stated frequency, not that it is reached always.
